blocks.text: Exception handling is used to manage errors that occur during program execution. It prevents the program from crashing and allows it to respond gracefully to unexpected situations. Proper exception handling improves program reliability and user experience. Python provides built-in tools to catch and handle exceptions efficiently.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Exception handling helps programs manage unexpected problems without stopping suddenly.

import sqlite3

try:
    # Connect to database
    connection = sqlite3.connect("school.db")
    cursor = connection.cursor()

    # Insert data into table
    cursor.execute("INSERT INTO students (ID, Name, Age) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", (1, "Ali", 20))

    # Save changes (ensures data integrity)
    connection.commit()
    print("Data inserted successfully")

except sqlite3.Error as e:
    # Handle database errors
    print("Error occurred:", e)
    connection.rollback()  # Undo changes if error occurs

finally:
    # Close connection
    if connection:
        connection.close()
        print("Connection closed")

items: try-except → handles errors and prevents crashes
rollback() → cancels changes if error occurs
